clue.text: Borderline case of aggression

parts.note: read as aggression that crosses a frontier: an army pushing over a border into another country

explanation.surface: A dispute that only just counts as hostility, a marginal instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borderline' seems to mean marginal or doubtful, but it means at the border: aggression across a national frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A military incursion into foreign territory is the classic act of aggression across a frontier.

clue.text: They come between Spain and France

definitions.text: They come between Spain and France

parts.words: They come between Spain and France
parts.note: read as a mountain range lying along the frontier separating the two countries, rather than people causing a rift

explanation.surface: Some troublemakers driving a wedge between two neighbouring nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come between' suggests people sowing discord, but it is literal geography: a mountain chain lies on the border.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain range forms the natural frontier separating the Iberian peninsula from France.

clue.text: Bird broke talon that was gold to start with

indicators.note: says the gold piece goes at the front, before the rest

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: the letters of talon are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird snapped a claw that had once been golden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start with' puts OR first, then 'broke' rearranges TALON into TOLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A small European bunting, once a prized delicacy, is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Greek character not having initially accepted dance

indicators.note: says the dance lacks a letter, which is then removed from it

parts.note: the lambada is a Brazilian dance

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of the word accepted

explanation.surface: A Greek person who refused at first to join a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' removes A (the first letter of 'accepted', picked by 'initially') from LAMBADA.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet is a character in that script.

clue.text: Father in charge in car club on the continent

indicators.note: puts the pieces before it inside the car club's letters

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is the British motoring organisation
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A priest running a motoring club somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a breakdown and motoring club.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is one of the world's seven great landmasses.

clue.text: Diminutive lady had terrible sensational book

parts.note: Penny is a pet form of the woman's name Penelope
dreadful means terrible

explanation.surface: A small woman owned an awful lurid novel.
explanation.walkthrough: A penny dreadful was a cheap, lurid Victorian serial story sold for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap Victorian thrillers of crime and horror were sold as these lurid serial publications.

clue.text: One who has been caught fighting

definitions.text: One who has been caught fighting

parts.words: One who has been caught fighting
parts.note: read as a soldier captured during combat and held by the enemy, rather than a brawler arrested

explanation.surface: Someone spotted in the middle of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught fighting' suggests being nabbed mid-brawl; it means taken captive during a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A combatant seized by the enemy in wartime is held as a captive until release.

clue.text: Likely to steal electrical device that had been touched

parts.note: a light is an electrical device such as a lamp
fingered means touched

explanation.surface: A lamp that has been handled is apt to go missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone with nimble hands given to pilfering.

clue.text: I talk foolishly about one who, in the main, is a thieving type

definitions.text: one who, in the main, is a thieving type

indicators.note: says the chattering word goes round the letter I

parts.note: to prate is to chatter foolishly

explanation.surface: I babble nonsense about a shady character at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PRATE round I. 'the main' is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea robber who plunders ships is a thief on the high seas.

clue.text: Steer to connect both sides of two universities

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated bull, an ox
to bridge is to span a gap joining two sides

explanation.surface: Guiding a link between opposing sides of two colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb meaning guide; it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The blend names Oxford and Cambridge together, England's two oldest universities.

clue.text: Nothing large in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Looking back, nothing big happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospect' reads L and IN backwards to give NIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A score of zero is a common sporting word for nothing.

clue.text: Having freedom of movement in American port

definitions.meaning: a port city on the Gulf coast of Alabama

explanation.surface: Free to travel around a harbour city in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to move freely, and also the name of an Alabama seaport city.

clue.text: Choice way to eat

parts.note: read as dining by picking separate dishes from a menu, rather than a fine way of eating

explanation.surface: An excellent manner of dining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choice' looks like an adjective meaning excellent; it means the diner chooses dishes individually.
explanation.definitionFit: This French menu phrase means ordering separately priced dishes rather than a set meal.

clue.text: Rod's signal

definitions.meaning: a prompt telling an actor to come in

explanation.surface: A stick that gives a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiards stick, and also an actor's prompt to begin speaking.

clue.text: Shabbiest basement converted not British

indicators.note: the remaining letters are converted into a new order
says one letter is left out of the word basement

explanation.surface: A grotty cellar has been done up, not in British style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes B from BASEMENT, and 'converted' rearranges the remaining ASEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Most mean can describe the poorest or most squalid, the most run-down.

clue.text: Oriental firm concerned with the environment

parts.note: E is short for East or eastern
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An Asian company with green credentials.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix signals ecological, as in green products and policies.

clue.text: A type of tank that's surgically sterile

parts.note: a septic tank holds sewage

explanation.surface: A kind of tank which is clean enough for an operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: A septic tank is a sewage tank, ironically the opposite of sterile.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of germs, as instruments must be in an operating theatre.

clue.text: To a remarkable extent sallying about

indicators.note: the letters of sallying are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Venturing out to an impressive degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of SALLYING.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means notably or conspicuously, often in 'signally failed'.

clue.text: Member of society not contributing

parts.note: read as someone who lives off others without giving back, like an organism feeding on a host

explanation.surface: A club member who fails to pay their subscription.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an unpaid club member; it means a sponger living off the community.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeloader who takes from the community without giving is likened to an organism feeding on a host.

clue.text: Fellow went to town in Surrey (not Esher initially) and found bird

indicators.note: says one letter is dropped from the Surrey town

parts.note: Reigate is a town in Surrey, a county south of London

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of the word Esher

explanation.surface: A man visited a Surrey town, skipped Esher, and spotted a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops E, the first letter of 'Esher' (picked by 'initially'), from REIGATE, a Surrey town. Esher is another Surrey town, a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The frigatebird is a large seabird of tropical oceans.

clue.text: One produces notes that others may play

definitions.text: One produces notes that others may play

parts.words: One produces notes that others may play
parts.note: read as someone who writes music for performers, rather than someone writing memos

explanation.surface: Someone writes messages for other people to act on.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of music creates scores that musicians perform.

clue.text: Control river pests

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
lice are parasitic pests

explanation.surface: Keep down the bugs along the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To police is to regulate or keep order, so it means to control.

clue.text: Mischievous child in blue found it was too small

indicators.note: places the child's letters inside the blue

parts.note: the sky is blue, and sky is a poetic word for blue
an imp is a naughty child

explanation.surface: A naughty boy in a blue outfit found it didn't fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty or skimped describes clothing or portions that are inadequate in size.

clue.text: Rover's outhouse?

parts.note: Rover is a British car make, so its outbuilding is where a car is kept, not a dog's kennel

explanation.surface: Where the family dog Rover sleeps outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover is a stock dog's name, so a kennel springs to mind; it is also a British car brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A building for housing a car stands beside many homes.

clue.text: Where there was no room in nazareth originally

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of nazareth

explanation.surface: The Nativity story: no space for Mary and Joseph in Nazareth.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Nativity, there was no room at the inn in Bethlehem; Nazareth is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Christmas story, Mary and Joseph were turned away from a lodging house.

clue.text: Make notes about spring inflation

indicators.note: the singing word goes about the water source

parts.note: to sing is to produce musical notes
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Jot down comments on rising prices in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' suggests writing; it means singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflation in the physical sense is puffing up, a growing bulge.

clue.text: Give confidence when certain

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Reassure someone when you are sure.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassure someone is to make them feel confident.

clue.text: Summed up about yield in the German returns

indicators.note: the reversed article goes round the surrender word
says the German article is read backwards

parts.note: der is a German word for the
to capitulate is to yield or surrender

explanation.surface: A summary of what the German side gave back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns DER into RED, and 'about' wraps RED around CAPITULATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to restate the main points briefly, to sum up.
